baseline.git_status: non-clean source-publication candidate working tree; reviewed bytes are recorded below and are not a clean accepted implementation

prior_design_draft.status: review draft only; not an implementation freeze

findings.finding: The draft names a source-catalog-v1 profile and .work/<batch>/source-catalog/catalog.json, but does not define a closed artifact schema, exact keys and row schemas, canonical encoding, profile/resource path, digest derivation, limits, staging API, fixed-slot state machine, status/query/resolve response schemas, or typed failure precedence.
evidence: prepare_catalog_material currently validates the closed ten-key legacy material (base_generation_material, base_tables, mapping, config, indexed_pages, compiled_pages, chunks, bm25, builder_files).
The existing base/search column manifests, SQL and generation profiles are separate legacy contracts and cannot supply the missing source-catalog contract or silently change column meaning.
findings.closure_action: Freeze a separate source-catalog-v1 schema and profile with exact object keys, row identities/order, JCS/LF bytes, digest inputs, byte/file/row limits and deterministic limit refusal. Specify create/reuse/conflict staging, complete status/query/resolve envelopes and stable error codes before implementation.

findings.finding: The existing collector deliberately refuses source-aware bytes with SOURCE_PROFILE_REQUIRED, while legacy catalog_status catches every ContractError and rewrites it to CATALOG_STALE. Routing the new source catalog through this interface would erase the required legacy refusal code.
evidence: collect_current_catalog_material calls require_legacy_profile before projecting rows; source-aware paths raise SOURCE_PROFILE_REQUIRED with exit code 75.
catalog_status catches that ContractError and raises CATALOG_STALE, so the old index.status behavior cannot be used as the source-catalog status implementation.
findings.closure_action: Keep legacy index/status and its SOURCE_PROFILE_REQUIRED behavior unchanged. Give source-catalog commands a separate collector/status path that preserves source-aware typed errors and does not wrap them in the legacy CATALOG_STALE adapter.

findings.finding: The existing retained snapshot is an optional collector return, not a closed build/status/query/resolve session. catalog_status retains and closes it around one call, while query_catalog calls catalog_status and then performs a second final catalog_status/collector pass.
evidence: _retain=True returns (material, _Snapshot), but the public collector otherwise closes its snapshot in the finally path.

query_catalog opens one live snapshot through catalog_status, reads the query inputs, then invokes catalog_status again for its final comparison; this violates the draft's one-snapshot promise if reused as-is.
findings.closure_action: Freeze one retained source-catalog session object whose named directory edges and bytes cover audit_integrity, source-state collection, complete inventory, projection reconstruction and citation resolution. Pass that session through build/status/query/resolve and perform one final complete-set/named-edge verification on every exit; never recursively reopen live authority.

findings.finding: The draft requires complete inventory and named-edge checks even when enumeration fails, but receipt_audit.audit_integrity's exception path only calls _Snapshot.verify. _Snapshot.verify compares snap.inventory only when _enumerate completed far enough to assign it.
evidence: _enumerate assigns snap.inventory only after _walk_inventory returns; a failure during _walk_inventory can leave inventory unset.
The BaseException path at audit_integrity:364-366 therefore checks tracked directories/files/absent slots but does not necessarily re-enumerate the complete set that the draft promises.
findings.closure_action: Define an explicit finalizer for the source-catalog session that records enumeration progress and runs a complete inventory/named-edge refusal check on both success and failure, including failure before initial inventory assignment. Preserve the original typed error unless the final safety check itself has a higher frozen precedence.

findings.finding: The draft requires generation provenance to cover the complete Vault inventory, source-catalog profile and resources, canonical schemas/taxonomy, implementation bytes, runtime/dependencies and tokenizer, but current inventory_digest and _generation do not define that source-catalog closure.
evidence: inventory_digest hashes sorted path/hash/size/mode rows, but the source catalog has not declared which retained paths, implementation/resources, profiles or dependency/tokenizer bytes participate in its digest.

_generation is explicitly tied to base-catalog-v1.generation-profile.json and produces a legacy projection-generation resource; it does not describe source-catalog-v1 or source-aware compiler/query semantics.
findings.closure_action: Freeze the complete generation material and its domain-separated digest: all retained head/receipt/current and historical snapshot rows, profile/schema/taxonomy/compiler/collector/query bytes, runtime/dependency/tokenization profiles and canonical projection rows. Reject any resource or row limit before omission; never truncate to fit.

findings.finding: Current source-state validation checks many associations, snapshots, Markdown locators and legacy code/PDF artifacts, but it does not define source-catalog rows for uncovered captures, unclaimed sources or source registrations without a canonical paper. It also has no public legacy code/PDF citation resolver with an explicit unsupported result.
evidence: audit_integrity reports unclaimed .raw/captured entries in orphans, while collect_source_state projects validated documents and rows without defining a visible uncovered result for those entries.

Markdown exact locator resolution exists, but code/PDF paths are validated through manifests/locators and do not expose the requested citation-resolution response shape; a source-catalog API must not fabricate text.
findings.closure_action: Freeze coverage/provenance rows for every source registration, capture and association, including explicit uncovered/orphan states. Require selected-display and citation-association references, exact raw path/hash/span/page/excerpt data, and a closed unsupported outcome for legacy code/PDF where exact resolution is unavailable.

findings.finding: The requested claim-text and source-excerpt lexical query is not the existing retrieval contract. retrieval.rank_hits ranks BM25 chunk hits with a stable (-score, paper_id, chunk_id) order and the legacy query response returns raw_hits/ranking plus generation digests; it does not define separate claim/source units or the new citation-bearing response.
evidence: mapping_from_database reconstructs legacy evidence units and chunk locators from the search schema.
query_catalog delegates ranking to bm25_query/rank_hits and returns raw_hits/ranking, with no source-catalog citation/association rows or claim/source excerpt index.
findings.closure_action: Freeze query input, tokenizer, normalization, score representation, ranking units, filters, top limits, tie order, digest binding and response/error schemas. Either explicitly reuse legacy BM25 semantics without changing legacy behavior or define a separate source-catalog ranker/index.

findings.finding: The draft's accepted/provisional/lifecycle filters need terminal assessment-head semantics, but existing query responses have no such filters and source-state exposes both claim-ledger assessment values and derived head event IDs without a source-catalog filter contract.
evidence: derive_assessment_heads derives the authoritative terminal event ID, while claim rows retain assessment/review fields and event actor/type lineage is separate.
No existing source-catalog query schema specifies whether accepted-only evaluates the terminal event, caller rows, lifecycle, or model/system provenance.
findings.closure_action: Define filter evaluation from the validated terminal assessment head and its event bytes, preserving actor/event lineage and reviewed_at. Accepted-only must reject or exclude provisional model/system claims and never promote a caller-supplied claim row.

findings.finding: Display selection and citation freshness are different identities. derive_display_heads returns a selected association reference, while Markdown locators bind their own association/raw bytes; using the selected display head as citation identity would mislabel valid historical citations stale.
evidence: A display head can roll back or select one association for a paper, independently of a claim locator that references another retained association.
The current state compiler validates association/raw-byte bindings, but no source-catalog row/result contract requires both selected_display_association and citation_association.
findings.closure_action: Freeze separate nullable display-head fields and per-citation association references. Citation validity must be determined from its exact retained association/history/raw bytes; display selection may be reported alongside it but cannot be used as freshness authority.

findings.finding: stage_bytes accepts an arbitrary relative path and verifies each call independently. It does not define the requested one retained source-catalog/catalog.json slot with absent/present identity, atomic create/reuse/conflict behavior and final exception verification.
evidence: The existing retained batch session protects checkout/.work/<batch> directory identities, but the source-catalog slot lifecycle and file identity are not a public contract.
Repeated stage_bytes calls could choose different paths or observe replacement between calls; the draft requires one fixed private path and one retained session.
findings.closure_action: Freeze a source-catalog staging API bound to .work/<batch>/source-catalog/catalog.json, with private mode, retained parent/slot identity, absent create, byte-identical reuse, differing-byte conflict and refusal on replacement/missing/symlink/hardlink/exception paths.

compatibility_findings: The draft correctly preserves the existing base-catalog-v1 and search-catalog-v1 schemas, SQL, column manifests and generation profiles; these must remain byte-compatible and separate from the new artifact.

_Snapshot, audit_integrity, source_state exact-byte validation, source-version display-head derivation, assessment-head derivation, Markdown locator resolution and retained batch staging are useful primitives for the successor contract after the missing session and schema boundaries are frozen.
The source catalog should remain a replaceable .work cache and must not mint receipts, mutate the Vault, create human review, change display decisions or become a second canonical ledger.
required_freeze_questions: What exact closed source-catalog-v1 artifact/profile and resource registry are authoritative, including canonical bytes, path, row schemas, ordering, digest domain and all limits?
What retained-session descriptor names every Vault ancestor directory, file, absent slot, current basis, historical snapshot and upstream/runtime/profile input through build/status/query/resolve?
What are the source-catalog status, exact-identity lookup, lexical query and citation-resolution response/error schemas, including legacy unsupported and uncovered cases?
What terminal assessment-head, lifecycle, display-selection and per-citation association semantics govern filtering and freshness?
What fixed-slot staging state machine and final success/exception verification enforce .work/<batch>/source-catalog/catalog.json?
required_acceptance_vectors: Empty Vault, receipt-backed fully rendered legacy, Markdown v2, mixed legacy/v2, repositories and historical ledger-snapshot catalogs produce closed deterministic rows and generation bytes.

Identical build/status/query/resolve inputs are byte-stable; a changed head, receipt, historical snapshot, source association, profile/resource, implementation byte, dependency/tokenizer profile or runtime makes the cache stale.
Unclaimed raw captures and registered sources without canonical paper produce visible uncovered rows; no source, association, citation, excerpt or unsupported result is silently dropped.
Markdown resolution round-trips exact Unicode spans and hashes; historical citation association remains valid across display rollback; changed raw bytes, association, page anchor or excerpt refuses.
Legacy PDF/code resolution uses retained parser/manifest bytes and established locator identity, otherwise returns the frozen unsupported result without fabricated text.
Assessment event forks, stale heads, model/system provisional claims and accepted-only filters exercise terminal-head semantics and preserve actor/event lineage.
Exact identity/title lookup and lexical ranking cover claim text and source excerpts with frozen tokenization, score, ties, limits, filters, result schema and generation/basis rechecks.

Source-catalog slot absent/create, byte-identical reuse, differing-byte conflict, parent replacement, slot unlink/recreate, symlink, hardlink, permission and exception paths refuse safely while preserving the original error precedence.
Loaded cache forgery, partial rows, invented excerpts, self-consistent descriptor hashes, unknown semantic paths and complete-set changes all refuse after reconstruction from retained source bytes.
The existing legacy index.status SOURCE_PROFILE_REQUIRED behavior, base/search resources and old query behavior remain unchanged.
